authoredFrom: SOL-1. Authored 2026-09-30 from the analyzer's own measured output for this file. The question is ownership: a `.sol` file is a COMPILATION UNIT holding several top-level declarations (OpenZeppelin's AccessControl.sol holds AccessControl AND AccessControlEnumerable), so the file's `module` symbol is the real owner of everything at file scope, and members carry `ownerName`.
note: `FILE_SCOPE_MAX` is a `constant_variable_declaration`, which grammar.js places in `_declaration` — FILE scope only. Inside a contract the same source text is a `state_variable_declaration`; the two are distinct node types and the corpus holds 6 and 352 of them respectively. `Owned.held` and `Owned.read` are contract members and are owned by `Owned`, not by the file. `FileScopeStruct.a` and `FileScopeEnum.ALPHA` are owned by their own type, which is the frame the declaration opens.

forbidSymbols.name: global
forbidSymbols.comment: SOL-1, and the reason this fixture exists. The pre-wave PowerShell lane spelled its file-scope edge source as the literal string `global`, and `isIndexArtifactName` (src/ast/analysis-exclusions.ts:129) REJECTS `global` as a symbol name — so not one of those edges could ever resolve to a stored symbol: measured at the store, 4 of 7 relationships on a two-file project had source_symbol_id = NULL. A synthesised global scope symbol is the same defect wearing a different language, and forbidding it by name is what pins the BEHAVIOUR rather than the intent.

expectRelationships.comment: A struct's member is owned by the STRUCT, not by the contract that contains the struct. The struct declaration opens a frame for exactly this.

SOL-13: a contract's member is owned by the CONTRACT. Compare the local `x` inside `fileScopeFunction`, whose own `contains` names the FUNCTION — Solidity locals are strictly function-scoped, so `contains module-owner-sol1.sol -> x` would be false.

SOL-2, pinned from the read position. A `identifier` whose PARENT is an `expression` is a read. Every declaration name in Solidity is the `name:` FIELD of its declaration node, so a declaration name can never sit under an `expression` and the two classes cannot overlap — which is why the rule is positional and not a name list. SUPERSEDED SPELLING (task-9 reconciliation, SOLIDITY-W8-CLAIM.md): this row pinned the BARE spelling of a function-scope binding read. The behaviour it pinned is now SUPERSEDED by the fleet binding claim (D7 CLAIMED, commit SOL-W8): a parameter/named-return read is published as `<declaring callable>\x00<binding name>` + metadata.localBinding, because the name has no published declaration and the bare spelling let the name-keyed resolver answer with a decoy. The construct the row tests is UNCHANGED — only its spelling moved. The old bare spelling is forbidden below so this fixture fails if the claim is ever removed.

SOL-12. Solidity has NO export construct, and the edge is still emitted: a `.sol` file's entire top-level surface is compiled into that unit's artifacts, so every file-scope declaration IS what the file offers its importers. Tier structural — the tree states which declarations are at file scope. `fileScopeFunction` is deliberately ABSENT from these rows: see expectRelationshipCount.

forbidRelationships.comment: The `global` scope source, forbidden by name. See forbidSymbols.

SOL-12, a stated boundary rather than an accident: the module's `exports` surface is the file-scope DECLARATION surface a compiler emits into the unit's ABI and abstractions. A free function is in the unit's bytecode but contributes no ABI entry, and publishing it as an export would claim a surface the language does not define. Counted below so a widening is visible.
SOL-13: `x` is a local of `fileScopeFunction`, and its own `contains` names the FUNCTION. A file-scope containment edge for a local would say the compilation unit contains it.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: Exactly the seven file-scope declarations that form the unit's ABI surface: one constant, one user-defined type, one struct, one enum, one error, one event, one contract. The free function is excluded (see forbidRelationships), which is why this is 7 and not 8 — a rule that exported every file-scope symbol would emit 8 and fail here.
